questions.q: What is the most common mistake that makes a load test misleading, according to this lesson?
options: Running the test from a data center geographically close to production
Hammering a single endpoint with uniform, identical requests and no variation, which measures something unrealistic rather than real production behavior
Using an open-source load testing tool instead of a commercial one
Running the test during business hours instead of overnight
questions.explain: A uniform synthetic stream against one endpoint measures how fast that path can serve unrealistic, perfectly uniform traffic — not how the system behaves under a real production mix — so it routinely passes while production falls over.

questions.q: Where should the request mix used in a realistic load test come from?
options: An even, equal-weight split across every known endpoint
The load testing tool's default sample traffic profile
A single endpoint believed to be the most performance-critical
Real access logs or APM traces, reproducing the actual distribution and relative frequency of endpoints hit in production
questions.explain: A load test that predicts production behavior starts from real production data — access logs or APM traces — reproducing the real skew in traffic rather than treating every endpoint as equally likely.

questions.q: Why does 'think time' matter in a realistic load test?
options: Think time has no measurable effect on test results and exists only for realism in reporting
Without it, real users would need to be interviewed before the test can run
Zero think time concentrates load unnaturally and can make connection pools and rate limiters behave differently than they would under real user pacing
Think time is only relevant for mobile applications, never for web backends
questions.explain: Real users pause between actions. A test with no think time concentrates requests unnaturally, which can distort connection pool and rate-limiter behavior compared to how the system actually experiences real user traffic.

questions.q: What specific class of failure is a soak test — a load test run at steady realistic load for an extended duration — designed to catch?
options: Failure modes that only appear after sustained operation, such as memory leaks, connection pool exhaustion, log disk fill-up, or token expiry under load
Typos in the load testing script's configuration file
Failures that only occur in the first ninety seconds of any test run
Whether the test's reporting dashboard renders correctly
questions.explain: An instant jump to peak load tests a different thing — absorbing a sudden spike. A soak test run at steady load for hours is specifically built to surface failures that only show up after sustained operation, like leaks or exhaustion, which a short test would never reveal.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a load test's result be treated as?
options: A number primarily useful for marketing claims about system speed
A real go/no-go signal about readiness — informed by realistic traffic, measured against latency percentiles, error rate, and resource utilization at the forecasted peak
A result to discard unless it matches the number expected ahead of time
A one-time check that never needs to be repeated as the system or its traffic changes
questions.explain: A realistic load test's output — p99 latency against its SLO target, error rate, and resource saturation at the forecasted peak plus headroom — is a real signal about production readiness, worth acting on before an event rather than discovering live.
